# Intake Brief — Text inputs miss keypresses when extension is syncing — pause sync while user is typing (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH)

## Problem statement

All in-extension screens that present a text input intermittently drop keypresses. The suspected cause is a background `wl sync` (and its follow-up list refresh/re-render) firing while the user is typing, contending for the TUI event loop or replacing render state mid-keystroke. There is no user value in syncing/refreshing while a form is active — it should be deferred until typing finishes.

## Users

- **Extension users typing in any form** — creators/editors filling fields in the Herdr worklist pane and any other in-extension overlay that accepts free-text input.
- **Operators triaging during incident flows** — users who rapidly fill forms while background workers run.

Example user stories:
- As a user filling the command-parameter form (`FormState` — unknown `<identifier>` prompts), I want every keystroke to register so I can submit the command without retyping.
- As a user writing a ship-it note / md note in the Ship-It dialog, I want the dialog to not lose characters when a periodic sync fires.
- As a user, I want the worklist to resume auto-sync/refresh promptly after I close the form, so I still see fresh data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Sync suppressed while typing:** While any text-input overlay is open, background `wl sync` is not spawned. Verified by running with `autoSync=true` and holding a form open for ≥2× `syncIntervalMs`: zero `wl sync` spawns (or, equivalently, the sync scheduler tick is skipped) — heartbeat/single-flight/visibility gates remain intact when not typing.
- [ ] **AC2 — Refresh/re-render suppressed while typing:** While any text-input overlay is open, auto-refresh list refetch/re-render is skipped so keypresses are not dropped. Verified by a deterministic unit/integration test that simulates rapid keystrokes into `FormState`/`ShipItDialogState` across a scheduled refresh tick — zero dropped characters; refresh resumes within one interval after the overlay closes.
- [ ] **AC3 — Coverage of all text-input screens:** The guard applies to every current text-input entry point (`form-dialog.ts` `FormState`, `ship-it-dialog.ts` `ShipItDialogState`, `md-note-edit.ts` note editing, and any other modal input) via a single shared predicate (e.g. `isTyping()` / `isInputActive()`) — not a per-screen copy-paste — so future inputs are covered by extending one place.
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression when not typing:** When no input is active, existing behaviour is unchanged: auto-refresh (30s default), auto-sync (60s default), visibility/heartbeat/DB-change gates, and downtime/mode-switch workers continue as before. Existing unit tests for `worklist.ts` / `auto-sync.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing & validation:** New unit tests cover: (a) sync tick skipped while form/ship-it dialog open; (b) refresh tick skipped while form/ship-it dialog open; (c) ticks resume after close; (d) typing simulation loses no keystrokes across ticks. A manual verification checklist is documented in a work-item comment (hold form open, observe no sync/refresh; close, observe resume).
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not regress existing gating: visibility (pause-when-hidden), single-flight, cross-instance heartbeat dedup, and DB-change skip must remain.
- Fix must be low-risk and narrowly scoped — gate the scheduler ticks, don't restructure the TUI event loop or form handling.
- Fire-and-forget sync semantics stay: skipping a tick is silent; no error surfacing while typing.
- Critical priority — dropped input is a data-loss-adjacent UX failure; prefer a minimal, reviewable patch.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` registers two periodic scheduler tasks: `refresh` (`autoRefresh`, 30s) and `sync` (`autoSync`, 60s, `fireImmediately:true`) which calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`. Both are visibility-gated (`paneGate.visible()`) but have no typing/input gate, so they fire even while `formState !== null` / `shipItDialog !== null`.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` provides `runSync` / `SyncTimer` with `ifIdle` single-flight and heartbeat dedup, but no caller-side typing guard.
- Text-input overlays: `form-dialog.ts` (`FormState.handleInput`/`render`), `ship-it-dialog.ts` (`ShipItDialogState`), `md-note-edit.ts` (note edit flow that opens a `FormState`). Keypress handling in `worklist.ts` correctly routes to `formState.handleInput` when open, but the background tick still runs concurrently.
- Related hardening exists: thrash prevention / lock-storm fixes (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E), idle-gated refresh (WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I), pause-when-hidden (WL-0MSB447GC0004CAW). None gate on typing.

## Desired change

- Introduce a single shared predicate (e.g. `isInputActive()` / `isTyping()`) that is true whenever any text-input overlay is open (`formState !== null || shipItDialog !== null || md-note-edit active || filter text input if applicable`), and check it at the top of the `refresh` and `sync` scheduler tick handlers (alongside the existing `paneGate.visible()` check) to skip `doSync`/`doRefresh` while typing. Record the decision to resume on close (next tick fires normally — no extra immediate refresh required, or document if one is desired).
- Ensure the guard also covers any other periodic background refresh that would cause a re-render/lost focus while typing (audit explicitly whether `downtimeWorker`/`modeSwitchWorker` need gating; if not, document why — they don't touch the list render path while a modal is open).
- Add unit tests for the typed-gating and a manual smoke checklist; update in-code comments and docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add typing/input gate to scheduler tasks (`refresh` and `sync` ticks) and define shared `isInputActive` predicate.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — No direct change expected, but verify `runSync` single-flight/heartbeat semantics are preserved; add comment if gating is caller-side.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — Defines `FormState`; reference for predicate coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog.ts` — Defines `ShipItDialogState`; reference for predicate coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-note-edit.ts` — Note-edit text input flow; ensure covered.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add typing-gated scheduler tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — Regression guard (no behaviour change when not typing).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Documents the typing gate (pause background work while a form is open).
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — Typing-gate behaviour + manual smoke verification procedure.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E — wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync (completed) — prior sync thrash hardening.
- WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I / WL-0MSB445BP0057ZQT — idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget (completed) — existing gating to extend.
- WL-0MSB447GC0004CAW — Docs & verification: pause-when-hidden behavior (completed) — visibility gate sibling.
- WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF — Selection list refreshes immediately when its tab/pane regains focus (completed) — refresh cadence context.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N — Pi extension polls even when selection list is not visible (completed) — similar "don't poll when not useful" pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Which screens count as "all in-extension screens that have text input"? — Answer (operator spec, WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH): All Herdr worklist pane overlays that accept free-text keystrokes via `FormState` / `ShipItDialogState` / `md-note-edit` (and any future text-input modal). Source: initial report "All in-extension screens that all text input will sometimes miss keypresses." No separate screen inventory was provided; brief assumes the three known overlays and a shared predicate to future-proof.
- Q: What exactly should be paused — `wl sync` only, or also list refresh / similar background work? — Answer (operator spec, WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH): "There is no need to do that (or similar) when the user is typing into a form in the extension." Interpreted as: at minimum suppress `wl sync` and the list `doRefresh` that would re-render/lose focus; audit other periodic ticks (downtime/mode-switch) and explicitly gate or document why not. Source: initial report sentence 2.
- Q: Should we debounce, buffer, or queue a refresh after typing ends? — Answer (Map, assumption — no producer input yet): Defer, don't queue: skip ticks while typing; next regular tick after close fires normally. If product wants an immediate post-close refresh, it can be added as a follow-up without changing the gating contract. Documented as assumption in Constraints/Desired change.
- Q: Is downtime-worker / mode-switch polling in scope for gating? — Answer (Map, assumption — to be confirmed in implementation): Out of scope for gating unless they trigger a list re-render or input loss; desired change asks for an explicit audit and doc note. No producer input; assumption will be validated in code review.

## Related work (automated report)

*Populated by `/skill:find-related` in step 7 — see work-item comments.*

## Implementation notes (audit remediation)

- The gate ordering lives in one exported `createGatedTick()` runner in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; both the `refresh` and `sync` tasks delegate to it. The scheduler-integration tests exercise this real runner via a real `TaskScheduler` (no inline re-implementation).
- Manual smoke checklist: see the work-item comment and the verification procedure in `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` (Typing gate section).

- Remediation 2026-09-13: scheduler-integration tests now exercise the exported `createGatedTick()` production runner via a real `TaskScheduler` (commit cf94be04); child AC reviews re-persisted after code/doc verification.

# Interview: LLM-Assisted Question Extraction

**Headline:** When `wl interview <id>` finds no parseable questions using the deterministic parser, optionally invoke a local LLM (via the existing embedding infrastructure) to extract unanswered questions from the description in free text.

## Problem Statement

The deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection` + `parseQAPairs`) requires an exact section header and rigid formatting. Real work items use varied formats (e.g., `## Appendix: Clarifying questions \& answers` with `- **Q1**: "..." — Answer (user@...): "..."). As a result, zero of the 17 `needsProducerReview=true` items are currently detectable. The original audit rejected WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 stating: "The command does not reliably detect questions."

An LLM normaliser turns this hard format dependency into a soft one — it can extract questions regardless of prose format.

## Users

- **Producers** running `wl interview <id>` — they want the command to find questions even when the description doesn't follow the canonical format.
- **Developers** — they want the feature to work with local models (Ollama/Foundry), not require a cloud API key.

**User Story:** "As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they're written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description."

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible embedding infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`.
- The LLM is asked to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
- Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively (same `createPromptLoop` readline flow) for confirmation and answer.
- Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the **deterministic re-serialiser** (`rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`) — never written directly from LLM output.
- When no LLM is available (no config, network failure, timeout), the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error.
- The LLM call is bounded: description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced.
- Tests cover: mock client returns valid questions, mock returns empty, mock throws error, no config available, timeout.

## Configuration

Opt-in via one of:
- `--llm` CLI flag: `wl interview <id> --llm`
- Config file: `intelligent: true` under `interview` section in `.worklog/config.yaml`

## Constraints

- No new dependencies — reuse `src/lib/search.ts` embedding infrastructure (OpenAI-compatible client, config resolution, graceful degradation).
- LLM is a *text completion* client, not an embedding client — but the same provider config, base URL, model, and auth apply. We should either:
  - (a) Add a `llm.*` config section parallel to `embedding.*`
  - (b) Or reuse the same provider config (the embedder already supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- The deterministic parser remains the primary path; LLM is strictly a fallback.
- Output is interactive-only (no --json mode for LLM calls).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — New `--llm` option, LLM client invocation, user confirmation loop for extracted questions.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `src/lib/search.ts` — Potentially add a `ChatClient` class alongside the existing `OpenAIEmbedder`, or reuse its config resolution for a completion client.
- `src/config.ts` — Add `interview.llm` or `llm.*` config schema.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — New test cases for LLM path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Model availability:** Not all setups have an LLM configured. Fallback must be silent and graceful.
- **Cost:** One completion call per invocation (~2-3 KB input) is cheap even at $0.001/call, but should be bounded.
- **Hallucination:** The mandatory user-confirmation step before writing to the description mitigates this.
- **Scope creep risk:** Users may want batch extraction across multiple items or LLM-generated answers. Track separately.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MULHNZBH001A9O1** – Tests: ChatClient injectable abstraction (blocked)
- **WL-0MQD1NPAD000O7OB** – Default config entries and child item updates (completed)
- **WL-0MLPRA0VC185TUVZ** – Item Details dialog not dismissed by esc (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alongside, already, answer (+162 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, already, answer, answers, api (+149 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, alongside, already, answer, apply (+135 more)

# Machine-Hygiene Skill — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

A global `machine-hygiene` skill that automates the manual performance-pressure analysis performed on 2026-09-27 (which resolved load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned `audit_runners` and stale vite servers). The skill provides a repeatable, safe diagnostic-and-remediation workflow for hosts running many concurrent pi agent sessions and test suites. It never acts autonomously without explicit producer approval.

**Headline:** Create the `machine-hygiene` global skill with a 6-step diagnostic-and-remediation workflow, configurable thresholds, before/after metric tables, and explicit approval gates before any destructive action.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs an automated, safe way to identify and resolve machine performance pressure without manually inspecting processes.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — can invoke the skill to auto-diagnose machine health during idle periods and report actionable findings.
- **Agents** — benefit from a cleaner, more responsive host machine when running multiple sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Global skill structure.** A skill named `machine-hygiene` exists under `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` with a `SKILL.md`, a `scripts/` directory, and tests per skill-authoring conventions. It is discoverable via `/skill: machine-hygiene`.

2. **AC2 — Diagnostic evaluation (Step 1).** The skill collects and renders a **before table** with the following metrics: load average (vs. core count), `/proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}` (percentages), free memory and swap usage, process and thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS (top 10), runnable process count, and stale device detection (zombie processes, stale files/locks). Each metric is classified as **low** (green), **warning** (amber), or **critical** (red) using configurable thresholds.

3. **AC3 — Pressure analysis (Steps 2–3).** The skill describes the primary pressures — identifying which processes/resources contribute most, their attributable ancestry (parent processes, systemd units, session IDs), and proposes concrete remediation actions (kill, renice, prune stale sessions, pace concurrent work), each with target PIDs/paths and expected impact.

4. **AC4 — Approval gate (Step 4).** The skill **stops** and presents findings to the operator/producer, awaiting explicit approval. No destructive action (kill, delete, modify) is taken before approval.

5. **AC5 — Conditional action (Step 5).** Only the explicitly approved subset of proposed actions is executed. The skill tracks which actions were approved vs. declined and reports accordingly.

6. **AC6 — After table (Step 6).** An **after table** is rendered alongside the before table showing current state for each metric, with per-metric priority annotations, and reports residual/legitimate load (e.g., active test suites, ongoing sessions).

7. **AC7 — Threshold configuration.** Low/warning/critical thresholds are configurable via a YAML config file (`~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml`) with documented sensible defaults. Defaults cover: CPU pressure (>70% warning, >85% critical), memory usage (>80% warning, >95% critical), I/O pressure (>50% warning, >80% critical), load average (>cores*0.7 warning, >cores*1.5 critical), zombie processes (>5 warning, >20 critical).

8. **AC8 — Tests.** Tests cover: threshold classification logic, the approval-gate refusal path (verify no destructive action without approval), metric collection on synthetic/fixture data, and config-file override behavior.

9. **AC9 — Documentation.** The skill is documented in `SKILL.md` with invocation examples, and is discoverable via `/skill: machine-hygiene`.

10. **AC10 — Full suite and documentation freshness.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, `SKILL.md`, and any relevant `docs/` entries), and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only by default.** Destructive actions (kill, delete, modify) are gated behind explicit operator/producer approval.
- **No direct .worklog mutation.** Any work-item side effects must use `wl` commands.
- **Reusable across projects.** Global skill under `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/`, with tests per skill-authoring conventions.
- **Process management scope only.** The skill focuses on process management (kill, renice, prune, pace). Resource-limiting via cgroups/systemd is out of scope.
- **Configurable thresholds.** Thresholds are configurable via YAML with sensible defaults.

## Existing State

- Manual machine-health analysis was performed on 2026-09-27, resolving load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned `audit_runners`, and stale vite servers.
- Related root causes are documented in:
  - `WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F` — debug-log rotation (audit debug log hygiene)
  - `WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS` — session close lifecycle (orphaned sessions, abandoned panes)
- Existing skills provide patterns: `cleanup` (branch pruning), `context-audit` (context measurement), and `heartbeat` (automated work monitoring).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — **new**: skill entry point with the 6-step workflow and approval gate
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/evaluate.py` — **new**: main entry point; orchestrates Steps 1–6
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py` — **new**: collects and classifies performance metrics (load, pressure, memory, swap, procs, RSS)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — **new**: analyses primary pressures, identifies root causes, proposes remediation actions
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/actions.py` — **new**: executes approved remediation actions (kill, renice, prune)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/scripts/tables.py` — **new**: renders before/after tables with status symbols
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — **new**: configurable thresholds with documented defaults
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — **new**: threshold classification and metric collection tests
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — **new**: pressure analysis and remediation proposal tests
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/tests/test_approval_gate.py` — **new**: approval-gate refusal tests

## Related Work

- `WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F` — Audit debug log retention (related: log-related resource consumption)
- `WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS` — Session close lifecycle (related: orphaned sessions, abandoned panes contributing to pressure)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/cleanup` — Branch cleanup skill (pattern reference for skill structure)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit` — Context measurement skill (pattern reference for metric collection)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/heartbeat` — Automated work monitoring (pattern reference for scheduled analysis)

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The skill runs on Linux with access to `/proc/pressure/` and standard process inspection tools (`ps`, `top`). Non-Linux platforms may need adaptation (documented as a follow-up).
- **Risk — false positives on RSS aggregation.** Per-command RSS grouping can be noisy when many instances of the same binary run under different names. Mitigation: group by process name (not command line) and show top 10 with individual PID breakdowns.
- **Risk — killing the wrong process.** Kill actions must include process ancestry verification (parent, session, uid) before execution. The approval gate requires operator confirmation for each kill.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Resource-limiting (cgroups, systemd) and I/O throttling are tempting but would significantly expand scope. Explicitly out of scope.
- **Risk — stale device detection accuracy.** Zombie processes and stale locks can be legitimate (e.g., during test teardown). The skill should flag rather than auto-remediate these; flagged items are always presented for approval, never auto-executed.
- **Scope-creep opportunity:** A scheduled cron-based auto-hygiene mode (runs at intervals, logs to a file) — captured as a linked follow-up, not in scope. This could be a separate `WL` child item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Skill name and location.** Should the skill be called `host-hygiene`, `perf-hygiene`, or `machine-hygiene`, and should it be global or project-scoped? **Answer (producer):** Proceed with `machine-hygiene` as a global skill under `~/.pi/agent/skills/`. **Final: `machine-hygiene`, global.**
- **Q2 — Threshold configuration.** Should thresholds be hardcoded, configurable, or both? **Answer (producer):** Proceed with configurable via YAML with sensible defaults. **Final: YAML config with documented defaults.**
- **Q3 — Action types beyond kill/prune.** Should the skill recommend resource-management actions like `nice`/`renice` or cgroup limits? **Answer (producer):** Focus on process management (kill, renice, prune, pace). cgroup/systemd resource-limiting is out of scope. **Final: process management only.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD** – Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (completed)
- **WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O** – Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W** – Recovery: classify 'All providers unavailable ... time window' 503 as SERVER_ERROR (open)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mujl1nah0042gos, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+238 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: action, actionable, active, agent, agents (+194 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mujl1nah0042gos, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+193 more)

# Core Skill Structure, Config & Documentation

## Summary

Create the global `machine-hygiene` skill skeleton with directory structure, SKILL.md entry point, and YAML threshold configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Skill directory exists.** `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` contains `SKILL.md`, `__init__.py`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, and `config.yaml`.
2. **AC2 — SKILL.md complete.** The skill entry point documents the 6-step workflow (diagnostic evaluation, pressure analysis, remediation proposal, approval gate, conditional action, after table), invocation examples, triggers ("machine hygiene", "machine-hygiene", "check machine health"), and lists all scripts.
3. **AC3 — Config.yaml with defaults.** `config.yaml` defines all threshold categories (cpu_pressure, memory_usage, io_pressure, load_average, zombie_processes) with low/warning/critical levels, each with documented values and units. Sensible defaults shipped: CPU pressure (>70% warning, >85% critical), memory usage (>80% warning, >95% critical), I/O pressure (>50% warning, >80% critical), load average (>cores*0.7 warning, >cores*1.5 critical), zombie processes (>5 warning, >20 critical).
4. **AC4 — Config loader.** A `load_config()` function in `scripts/config.py` reads the YAML file from `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` and returns a dict. Default values are used for any missing keys.
5. **AC5 — Discoverable.** The skill front-matter has `name: machine-hygiene` and a meaningful `description`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Create directory structure: `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/{scripts,tests}`
2. Create `__init__.py` (empty)
3. Create `config.yaml` with all threshold categories and defaults
4. Create `SKILL.md` with 6-step workflow description, invocation examples, script inventory
5. Create `scripts/config.py` with `load_config()` function

## Deliverables

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` directory with all scaffold files
- `config.yaml` with documented defaults
- `SKILL.md` with full workflow documentation
- `scripts/config.py` with config loader

# Metrics collection module

## Summary

Implement the metrics collection module that gathers system performance data and classifies each metric against configurable thresholds.


## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1** — AC1 — \`metrics.py\` collects all required metrics: load average vs core count, /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io} percentages, free memory and swap usage, process and thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS top 10, runnable process count, and stale device detection (zombie processes, stale files/locks).
2. **AC2** — AC2 — Each metric is classified as low/warning/critical using thresholds from the config file.
3. **AC3** — AC3 — \`collect_metrics()\` function returns a dict of metric_name → {value, status, description} suitable for table rendering.
4. **AC4** — AC4 — When /proc/pressure/ is unavailable (non-Linux), graceful fallback with a warning is returned without crashing.
5. **AC5** — AC5 — RSS aggregation groups by process name (not command line) and shows top 10 with individual PID breakdowns.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Create \`scripts/metrics.py\` with functions: \`collect_metrics()\`, \`classify_metric(value, thresholds)\`, \`_read_proc_pressure()\`, \`_get_process_stats()\`, \`_get_rss_top10()\`, \`_detect_stale_devices()\`
2. Import config from \`scripts/config.py\` for threshold values
3. Handle missing /proc/pressure/ gracefully (non-Linux)
4. Group RSS by process name, show top 10 with PID breakdowns
5. Return structured dict ready for table rendering

## Deliverables

- scripts/metrics.py with all collection functions

# Pressure analysis & remediation

## Summary

Implement pressure analysis that identifies root causes of performance pressure and proposes concrete remediation actions with risk assessments.


## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1** — AC1 — \`pressure_analysis.py\` identifies the primary pressure source(s) from the metrics collected in Feature 2.
2. **AC2** — AC2 — For each pressure source, the skill identifies attributable ancestry: parent processes, systemd units, session IDs.
3. **AC3** — AC3 — Concrete remediation actions are proposed for each pressure source (kill, renice, prune stale sessions, pace concurrent work), each with target PIDs/paths and expected impact.
4. **AC4** — AC4 — Each action includes a risk assessment (low/medium/high) based on process ancestry verification (parent, session, uid).
5. **AC5** — AC5 — Actions are ranked by impact-to-risk ratio for operator consideration.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Create \`scripts/pressure_analysis.py\` with functions: \`analyze_pressures(metrics)\`, \`find_ancestry(pid)\`, \`propose_remediations(pressures)\`, \`rank_actions(actions)\`
2. Use /proc filesystem and ps for process ancestry information
3. Cross-reference with systemd unit information where available
4. Generate structured action proposals with risk scores

## Deliverables

- scripts/pressure_analysis.py with analysis and proposal functions

# Table rendering & approval gate

## Summary

Implement before/after table rendering with status symbols and an approval gate that halts execution before any destructive action.


## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1** — AC1 — \`tables.py\` renders a **before table** showing all metrics with their values, status symbols (green/amber/red), and priority annotations.
2. **AC2** — AC2 — \`tables.py\` renders an **after table** alongside the before table, showing current state for each metric after actions.
3. **AC3** — AC3 — Status symbols: 🟢/low, 🟡/warning, 🔴/critical (with ASCII fallback: OK/WARN/CRIT).
4. **AC4** — AC4 — After table reports residual/legitimate load (active test suites, ongoing sessions) to avoid suggesting remediation on active work.
5. **AC5** — AC5 — The approval gate in the main script **stops** before any destructive action and presents the before table, pressure analysis, and proposed actions to the operator.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Create \`scripts/tables.py\` with functions: \`render_before_table(metrics)\`, \`render_after_table(before, after)\`, \`render_proposed_actions(actions)\`
2. Use Unicode status symbols with ASCII fallback
3. Integrate legitimate-load detection (active sessions, test suites) into after table
4. Implement approval gate in main evaluate.py as a distinct step that halts execution

## Deliverables

- scripts/tables.py with rendering functions

## Goal

Add a `ChatClient` (OpenAI-compatible chat-completions client) alongside `OpenAIEmbedder` in `src/lib/search.ts`, resolving the existing `llm.*` configuration, so the interview command can obtain a text completion without new dependencies.

Parent: WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF (interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ChatClient` is exported from `src/lib/search.ts` with `readonly available: boolean` and `complete(prompt: string): Promise<string>`.
- The constructor resolves provider settings via the existing `resolveLlmConfig()` (`llm.*` config, `LLM_*` env vars, built-in defaults) and/or accepts injected `{ baseUrl, model, apiKey, timeoutMs, hasExplicitConfig }`.
- `available` is `false` when no `llm.*` config and no `LLM_*` env var is present; `complete()` throws before attempting any network call when unavailable.
- `complete()` POSTs to `${baseUrl}/chat/completions` with a `{ model, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }] }` body and returns the first choice's message content; the `Authorization` header is sent only when `apiKey` is non-empty (supports local providers such as Ollama).
- The configured `timeoutMs` is enforced via `AbortController`; a non-2xx response throws an error including the HTTP status and a bounded (<=200 char) response body.
- `tests/lib/llm.test.ts` (WL-0MUQ0VO7O0000XIC) passes; no existing test regresses.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the `ChatClient` class to `src/lib/search.ts`, mirroring `OpenAIEmbedder`'s config precedence and conditional-auth header logic.
- Use the global `fetch` + `AbortController`; no new dependency.
- Export the class and any needed types.
- Keep the deterministic/local-first behaviour: no API key required.

## Key Files

- `src/lib/search.ts`
- `src/config.ts` (`resolveLlmConfig` — reference)
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` (`LlmConfig` — reference)
- `tests/lib/llm.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Working, tested `ChatClient` matching the WL-0MUQ0VO7O0000XIC contract.

## Dependencies

- WL-0MUQ0VO7O0000XIC — ChatClient contract tests.

data.title: Interview LLM-extraction tests

data.description:
## Goal

As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the command to fall back to a local LLM to extract clarifying questions when the deterministic parser finds none, so I can answer questions written in natural prose without manually searching the description.

Parent: WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF (interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `InterviewOptions` in `src/cli-types.ts` gains `llm?: boolean`; `wl interview <id> --llm` parses and enables the fallback. Enablement is `--llm` OR `interview.intelligent: true` (`--llm` wins).
- When the deterministic parser finds no questions, and the `--llm` flag is set (or `intelligent: true` in config), the command calls a local LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible infrastructure `src/lib/search.ts`, asking it to return a JSON array of `{ question: string }` objects extracted from the description, or an empty array if none found.
- The LLM call is bounded: the description is truncated to 8 KB, a timeout of 15 seconds is enforced, and the LLM is never called when the deterministic parser finds questions.
- The response is parsed defensively — non-JSON, non-array, or malformed entries are treated as "no questions" without throwing.
- Each extracted question is presented to the user interactively via the same `createPromptLoop` readline flow for confirmation and answer (parent AC3).
- Only confirmed questions are written to the description using the deterministic re-serialiser `rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`; raw LLM output is never written directly (parent AC4).
- When no LLM is available (no `llm.*` config, no `LLM_*` env), or on network failure / timeout / non-2xx, the command falls back to the existing deterministic-only message with no error and the same exit code as today (parent AC5).
- The LLM path is interactive-only: `wl interview` still rejects `--json` with `requires-tty` before any LLM call, so no LLM output is emitted in JSON mode (parent constraint).
- `CLI.md` documents the `--llm` flag and the `interview.intelligent: true` config opt-in, including that provider settings come from `llm.*`.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (WL-0MUQ0VPQ7000TH98) passes; the full suite passes; no existing test regresses.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/commands/interview.ts`: add the `--llm` option and an injectable `ChatClient` seam; extend `runInterview` (or add a fallback step) to call the LLM when the deterministic parser yields nothing, parse the JSON defensively, and drive the existing confirmation loop.
- Reuse `extractClarifyingSection` for the section body when present; otherwise use the whole description; truncate to 8192 bytes in both cases.
- Build the description update with `rebuildQAPairs` / `rebuildDescription`; insert a clarifying-questions section header only when none exists (keep re-runs idempotent).
- `src/cli-types.ts`: add `llm?: boolean` to `InterviewOptions`.
- `CLI.md`: add the flag/config documentation.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts`
- `src/cli-types.ts`
- `src/lib/search.ts`
- `src/config.ts`
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`
- `CLI.md`

## Deliverables

- Opt-in LLM-assisted question extraction with interactive confirmation, deterministic write-back, and silent graceful degradation.
- Updated CLI documentation.

## Dependencies

- WL-0MUQ0VPQ7000TH98 — Interview LLM-extraction tests.

# Plan: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback

## Seed Context

- **Work item:** WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF — interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback
- **Type:** feature | **Priority:** high | **Effort:** Small | **Risk:** Medium
- **Stage at planning start:** intake_complete
- **User story:** As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they are written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description.

### Reusable infrastructure found (no new dependencies)

- `src/lib/search.ts` — `OpenAIEmbedder`: OpenAI-compatible HTTP client with conditional `Authorization`, `available` flag, graceful degradation.
- `src/config.ts` — `resolveLlmConfig()` and the `llm.*` schema already exist (`llm.baseUrl|model|apiKey|timeoutMs`; `LLM_BASE_URL|LLM_MODEL|LLM_API_KEY|LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`; defaults: herdr proxy `http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1`, model `compact`, 15 s timeout).
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection`, `parseQAPairs`) and lossless re-serialiser (`rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription`) remain the primary path and the write-back safety net.
- `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts` — existing `llm.*` config test patterns to mirror.

## Decisions (interview)

| # | Question | Answer | Rationale |
|---|----------|--------|-----------|
| 1 | Reuse `llm.*` config or add `interview.llm`? | **(a) Reuse `llm.*`** | One provider section, already implemented and tested; no new provider config surface. |
| 2 | ChatClient design? | **(a) New `ChatClient` class** alongside `OpenAIEmbedder` in `src/lib/search.ts` | Follows the blocked ChatClient work item (WL-0MULHNZBH001A9O1) intent; clean injectability for unit tests. |
| 3 | Model selection? | **(a) Reuse existing default** (`compact` via `llm.*`) | Consistent with the rest of the system; override remains possible via `llm.model` / `LLM_MODEL`. |

**Documented assumption (agent):** the LLM fallback triggers when `parseQAPairs` returns zero questions, whether or not a recognised section header exists. When no section header is found the LLM scans the whole description (truncated to 8 KB). This matches AC2 ("extracted from the description") and the problem statement (varied/unparseable formats). No requirement is invented beyond this reachability interpretation.

## Feature plan (vertical slices, test-first)

| # | Feature | Type | Depends on |
|---|---------|------|------------|
| F1 | ChatClient contract tests | task | — |
| F2 | ChatClient implementation | task | F1 |
| F3 | Interview LLM config schema | task | — |
| F4 | Interview LLM-extraction tests | task | F2, F3 |
| F5 | Interview LLM fallback integration | feature | F4 |

Test-first ordering holds: F1 (tests) precedes F2 (impl); F4 (tests) precedes F5 (impl). Each item carries code, tests, and (where relevant) docs so every phase is end-to-end.

## Vertical slice verification

Each feature cuts through all relevant layers:

- **F1/F4** — tests (contract + command-level) only, by design (test-first).
- **F2** — library code (`search.ts`) + tests + config resolution integration.
- **F3** — types (`packages/shared/src/types.ts`) + config validation (`src/config.ts`) + tests.
- **F5** — CLI option (`cli-types.ts`, `interview.ts`) + user interaction (readline confirm loop) + config enablement + docs (`CLI.md`) + tests.

No horizontal-only (layer-by-layer) phase exists.

## Phasing guidance

Between phases, the implementing agent must re-read the next work item's description and update it if the preceding phase changed assumptions (e.g. the exact `ChatClient` constructor signature pinned by F1/F2 feeds F4/F5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Config reuse — The existing `llm.*` config section in `.worklog/config.yaml` (with `LLM_*` env vars) is already in place. Should the interview command reuse this (`llm.*` section, `LLM_*` env vars) for its LLM call, or should we create a separate `interview.llm` config section?" — Answer (operator): **(a) Reuse `llm.*`**. Evidence: `src/config.ts` `resolveLlmConfig()`; `packages/shared/src/types.ts` `LlmConfig`; `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts`. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-01.
- Q: "ChatClient design — The related work item (WL-0MULHNZBH001A9O1) references a `ChatClient` injectable abstraction, but it is blocked with an orphaned parent. The existing `OpenAIEmbedder` calls `/embeddings`; we need `/chat/completions`. Which design?" — Answer (operator): **(a) New `ChatClient` class** alongside `OpenAIEmbedder` in `src/lib/search.ts`. Evidence: WL-0MULHNZBH001A9O1 (blocked); `src/lib/search.ts` `OpenAIEmbedder`. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-01.
- Q: "Model selection — The existing LLM config defaults to model `compact` at the herdr proxy. Question extraction may benefit from a more capable model. Which default?" — Answer (operator): **(a) Reuse the existing default model** (`compact` if using `llm.*` config). Evidence: `src/config.ts` `DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL = 'compact'`. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-01.

No OPEN QUESTION entries remain. No producer review required.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-01 — Initial decomposition into 5 vertical-slice items (F1–F5); dependencies wired; interview decisions recorded. Author: plan skill (agent).
